transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-05-18 09:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Claire (Horizon DataWorks - Head of ML), Devon (Platform Eng), Rina (PM)

Auto-generated summary: quick kickoff to align on POC success metrics, define golden prompts and regression plan, and size workload for benchmark runs.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, golden prompt set, hallucination/format checks, scoring rubric, timelines

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll give a short agenda. this is Maya from Redwood, with Luis and Samir on the engineering side. who we have on the horizon side?
00:07 Claire: Claire here, hi. hi Maya.
00:09 Devon: Devon. good morning.
00:10 Rina: Rina. thanks for setting up.
00:15 Maya: great. goal for today is to align on POC acceptance criteria and the quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression checks, the usual. we'll also need to size the load for our benchmarks so we can provision Dedicated nodes for the runs.
00:28 Luis: one quick note; sometimes I call out model variants as, as the redwood models or the, the open quantized ones q4 and q8, but forgive the shorthand, we'll spell them out in the doc.
00:36 Claire: yeah that's helpful. our main objective is to replace a rule-based tagging pipeline with an LLM, so success is both precision on labels and throughput under our peak hours.
00:48 Rina: timeline question, we have a board review at the end of June, so we wanted a POC report before then. ideally mid-June finish?
00:56 Maya: ok mid-June is doable; this gives us about four weeks. we'll propose a 3-week active testing window plus a one-week buffer for regression and final report.
01:05 Claire: good. on metrics, we care about: F1 per label, macro F1, false positive rate for high-risk classes, and hallucination incidence when system invents facts. also latency P95 under load.
01:18 Luis: noted. for hallucination checks we'll add both open-ended prompts to detect made-up facts and structured format checks so the model can't return malformed JSON that breaks pipeline.
01:28 Devon: can you explain what you mean by format checks? we had issues where the model returned a list of tags as a string blob and our parser choked.
01:35 Samir: yes, we'll include strict schema validation. approach: golden prompt will include explicit instruction + example outputs; the scoring pipeline will parse generated output and run schema validators. failed parses count as a type of failure in the metrics.
01:49 Claire: for golden prompts, we want around 120 golden examples covering edge cases — low-resource labels, nested entities, and ambiguous contexts. is that enough to catch regressions?
01:59 Luis: 120's a sensible start; for regression coverage we usually keep a golden set of ~100-200 examples and a larger validation corpus of a few thousand cases sampled from production. regressions run nightly in the POC and we'll run a full sweep before handoff.
02:13 Rina: we also need to capture label explainability; product demands a human-readable justification for high-impact labels. can the model emit a short rationale?
02:22 Samir: yes, we'll add a 'rationale' field in the output schema. we'll measure alignment by token overlap and by reviewer scoring on 50 sampled rationales. manual review budget?
02:31 Claire: we can allocate two ML engineers to review 50 items — that's feasible.
02:35 Maya: great. on workload sizing — Devon, can you describe your peak QPS and payload size?
02:41 Devon: sure. normal day is 120 requests per minute, burst up to 800 rpm during our evening ingestion window, payload average is 1.8KB per request but some docs are long up to 20KB.
02:53 Luis: ok we need to simulate both avg and tail token lengths. we'll do three benchmark profiles: nominal (120 rpm, avg tokens), peak (800 rpm, mixed token sizes), and stress (1k+ rpm sustained for short window).
03:07 Maya: for the initial POC runs we recommend 24-hour soak for nominal, two 2-hour peak windows, and a single stress test. does that match your ops constraints?
03:17 Devon: yes, we can schedule during our maintenance windows, prefer weekends for stress.
03:21 Rina: what about privacy, we cannot send PHI to hosted endpoints. this is partly why we're evaluating Dedicated capacity or Private.
03:28 Maya: totally understood — we will scope both hosted (with synthetic data) and Dedicated/private with direct data routing. in the SOW we'll include steps for on-prem or VPC connector if you need KMS/HSM integrations.
03:40 Claire: and compliance—SOC2 plus audit logs are required. we need to see retention configs and access logs.
03:46 Luis: we'll attach our security pack. for the benchmark we can run in a dedicated environment with audit logging enabled.
03:53 Rina: ok good. scoring approach — how will you aggregate quality metrics into a pass/fail for the POC?
04:00 Samir: proposed acceptance criteria: macro F1 >= 0.78, per-critical-label F1 >= 0.70, hallucination rate < 2% on golden set, parse success rate > 99%, latency P95 < 300ms on nominal and < 450ms under peak. these are starting thresholds.
04:17 Claire: macro F1 0.78 is ok as a starting point but for top labels we'd like 0.8+. are thresholds flexible?
04:23 Maya: yes flexible — we'll work with you to set final targets in the SOW based on initial benchmark outcomes. we'll also report cost-per-1000 tokens and provide model switch recommendations to hit cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:36 Devon: about regression tests, do you run automated reruns when we push new prompts or changes?
04:41 Luis: yes within the POC we'll set up a regression pipeline that re-runs the golden set and the nightly sample. any model or prompt changes that drop metrics beyond a guardrail will create an alert and optional auto-rollback.
04:53 Rina: what's the guardrail delta? like how much drop before rollback?
04:57 Samir: we suggest per-metric delta thresholds e.g. > 3% absolute drop in macro F1 or > 1% increase in hallucination triggers a hold. we'll propose defaults but you can tune.
05:08 Claire: how do you measure hallucination? just NER false positives or factual fabrications?
05:13 Luis: two signal approach — for structured labels we treat extraneous invented entities as hallucinations; for factual claims we run a lightweight fact-checker against known KB where feasible and mark ambiguous items for manual review. golden set also includes known-fact prompts.
05:27 Rina: edge case: when model returns plausible but incorrect label, that's subtle. how will reviewers mark that?
05:33 Samir: we'll have a 3-point reviewer rubric: correct / partially-correct (requires human patch) / incorrect. scoring maps partially-correct as 0.5. we'll include this in the scoring spreadsheet.
05:44 Maya: timeline recap: today align on scope; by Thu Maya shares benchmark template; Devon provides QPS and data samples by Fri; initial synthetic bench runs next week; active testing window week of 2027-06-01 with final report mid-June.
05:58 Claire: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side?
06:01 Luis: need data sample (anonymized) and confirmation of retention rules. also decision on Dedicated vs Private for live data.
06:10 Rina: we'll confirm retention and share a small anonymized dataset.
06:14 Maya: ok next steps and I'll follow up with SOW draft.

Action items recapped in call:
- Maya: share benchmark spreadsheet and SOW draft (due 2027-05-20)
- Devon: provide QPS numbers, token distributions, and data sample (due 2027-05-21)
- Luis: initial model/quantization config and infra estimate (due 2027-05-24)
- Claire & Rina: finalize acceptance thresholds with product & security (due 2027-05-25)

End of transcript
